newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi seeks to oust his trial judge.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi seeks to oust his trial judge.

text.p: Italy's former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi has asked for the judge at his corruption trial to be dismissed for alleged bias.

The 60-year-old media billionaire, who is accused of complicity in bribery of tax officials, outlined his case against presiding judge Carlo Crivelli in an 11-page deposition lodged on Saturday with the Court of Appeal in Milan.

Made available to journalists, it reports a private exchange of remarks between Crivelli and prosecutor Gherardo Colombo on September 18 in which Berlusconi alleges the judge refers to "carrot and stick" tactics in the conduct of the trial.
The remarks, made in court but outside formal proceedings, were picked up by courtroom microphones and transcribed.
Berlusconi alleged that they were "irreconcilable with the impartiality and objectivity that are essential hallmarks of a judge" and asked the Court of Appeal to have Crivelli removed.
If his challenge is accepted by the court the trial, which began on January 17, would have to start again.

The suit revived claims that Berlusconi, prime minister for seven stormy months in 1994, has levelled throughout his judicial battles that the cases against him amount to a plot to ruin both him and his giant Fininvest media and business empire.

It coincides with suggestions that the tycoon-turned -politician may be losing his grip on leadership of Italy's centre-right Freedom Alliance since its defeat in last April's general election to a centre-left "Olive Tree" coalition.

Giuliano Urbani, a senior figure in Berlusconi's conservative Forza Italia party, was quoted on Sunday as saying the mogul was increasingly isolated in the Freedom Alliance, whose partners range from centrists to the hard right.

"Berlusconi hasn't understood that his allies are all reasoning with the certainty that he isn't the leader of the Alliance any more," L'Unita, the newspaper of the large leftist PDS party, quoted Urbani as saying in an interview.
Berlusconi's trial in Milan is the first of several investigations against him by Milan's elite pool of anti-graft investigators to come to court.

He is accused of having conspired in the payment to tax officers of alleged bribes totalling 380 million lire ($250,000) by four of his companies for lenient audits or other concessions between 1989 and 1981.
Berlusconi has denied knowledge of the payments at the time they were made and argues that they were extorted. Others on trial with him include his younger brother Paolo.
Neither Crivelli nor Colombo, one of the stars of the Milan pool, has commented on Berlusconi's suit.
Berlusconi's political profile has been noticeably lower since April and his defeat in the general election.

On the business front, he has reduced his holding in his Mediaset television company through a share offer in order to answer conflict of interest criticism. New media legislation drafted by the government could also affect his business.
